deep.reconstruction:
This page continues an expository introduction. The neighbouring pages and the cote ('laïus novembre-décembre 1967, Cristaux') identify it as a manuscript draft of the introduction to Grothendieck's IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (published in 'Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas', 1968). The purpose is to motivate a p-adic cohomology theory.

Argument on this page, in modern terms:
(1) Characteristic 0 (continued from p.9). For X of finite type over a field of characteristic 0, the comparison H^i(X,Z_l) = H^i(X^an,Z) ⊗ Z_l transfers integral information. If f is an endomorphism (or a Frobenius-type operator in the number-field setting), the characteristic polynomial of f on H^i(X,Z_l) equals that on H^i(X^an,Z). It therefore has integer coefficients independent of l.
(2) Characteristic p > 0. There is no transcendental integral cohomology to compare with, so the situation is much worse.
 - Finiteness: H^i(X,Z_l) is of finite type because each H^i(X,Z/l^n) is finite. In 1967 this was proved only for X proper or dim X ≤ 2 (dim 2 via resolution of surfaces). Grothendieck says that in general resolution of singularities seems to be needed.
 - Independence of l: even for X smooth projective, it was unknown whether the rank of H^2(X,Z_l) is independent of l. A fortiori it was unknown whether the characteristic polynomials of f have integer coefficients independent of l.
 - He states that these are consequences, not yet proved, of a solution of the Weil conjectures.
(3) He begins the reduction: tensor with Q_l. The next page continues: one then asks whether the coefficients are in Q, which is a Lefschetz-type problem on algebraic cycles (the standard conjectures). Even if this were solved, l ≠ p would give only coefficients in Z[1/p]. This is the 'paradox' that shows the need for a p-adic cohomology.
errors: The guess that resolution of singularities seems necessary for finiteness of H^i(X,Z/l^n) for non-proper X in characteristic p turned out to be wrong. Deligne's 'Théorèmes de finitude en cohomologie l-adique' (SGA 4½, 1977) proves finiteness for separated schemes of finite type over a field (l ≠ p) without resolution. This is a historically accurate statement of the 1967 state of knowledge, not an error at the time.

Minor point: independence of l for Betti numbers of smooth projective varieties follows from Deligne's Weil I (1974). Independence of l for arbitrary (non-proper, singular) X is still not fully known for individual H^i (Weil II gives the compactly supported, alternating-sum results). The phrase 'consequences of a solution of the Weil conjectures' is therefore accurate only for the smooth projective case.

ideas.what: Integrality and l-independence of characteristic polynomials of endomorphisms on l-adic cohomology in characteristic 0, via comparison with singular cohomology
ideas.modern_name: Artin comparison theorem; l-independence via Betti cohomology

ideas.where_published: Introduction to 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); SGA 4

deep.surprise_reason: This is a manuscript draft of the published introduction to the 1967 'Crystals' lectures, stating the well-known 1967 state of the art. The only mild historical interest is the explicit expectation that resolution of singularities would be needed for l-adic finiteness in the non-proper case, which Deligne later bypassed.
transcription_corrections: 'On peut commencer par [...] terminer[?] par Q_l' should read 'On peut commencer par tensoriser par Q_l' (a crossed-out word precedes it).

'Cela [-serait-] conséquences d'ailleurs {+sont+}, actuellement, ([-le plus-] plus importante[?] pas encore démontrée[?] d'une solution[?] des conjectures de Weil' is roughly: 'Ce sont d'ailleurs, actuellement, (les) plus importantes conséquences pas encore démontrées d'une solution des conjectures de Weil' (with crossed-out 'serait' and 'le plus').

The finiteness sentence reads: 'n'est prouvé que si X est propre ou si dim X ≤ 2 — pour l'avoir en général, il semble qu'il faille la résolution des singularités'. The '— pour' sits at the end of the line containing 'dim X ≤ 2'.
'si les coefficients[?] des polynômes plus haut sont entiers[?]' is plausibly '...si les coefficients des polynômes envisagés plus haut sont entiers et indépendants de l' (partly illegible).
